drafted_from: tool:measure-loudness's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/measure-loudness.mjs, and the script run on a synthetic 7 second tone clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Is my video loud enough to publish? Measure its loudness against -14 LUFS." It runs tool:measure-loudness and says whether it passes and why not.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name by its file identity and answers from that video alone, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find your video's identity in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.
2. Say "Measure this video's loudness" with that identity. Add target_lufs if your site wants something other than -14.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:measure-loudness. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.ok and result.reasons (for example too-quiet), with integrated_lufs, lra_lu and true_peak_dbfs. If it is off, fix it with tool:mix-sound-layers and loudness_lufs.

worked_examples.ask: Is this video loud enough to publish?
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/measure-loudness.mjs and run on a 7 second 440 Hz tone clip at default level, target -14
